title: Kattegattleden: Gothenburg to Helsingborg

bestPeriod.window: May to late September; warmest swimming July-August; best light and empty roads late August-mid September
bestPeriod.raw: May to late September; warmest swimming July-August; best light and empty roads late August-mid September

accommodation.note: €95-170 per night, double; STF hostels €40-60 pp; two seaside spa nights push the top end

food.note: €50-75 per day (bakery breakfast, harbour lunch, one proper dinner)

transport.note: €150-220: bike hire €120-160 for the week, plus one-way rail return Helsingborg-Gothenburg

profile.difficultyNote: Easy. Sweden's flattest long-distance route; 45-70 km per day, rarely more than 250 m gain, one real climb over Hallandsåsen

summary: A seven-day cycling trip itinerary in Halland & northwest Skåne coast, Sweden.

itinerary.title: Gothenburg to Kungsbacka
itinerary.morning: Collect touring bikes in central Gothenburg, reserve panniers and a rear rack explicitly, most shops rent them separately. Coffee at Da Matteo in Magasinsgatan before you roll.
itinerary.afternoon: Out through Askim and Billdal on segregated cycleway, then the coastal stretch past Särö Västerskog nature reserve, a rare wind-sculpted oak forest on the shore. Swim stop at Vallda Sandö if the wind is off the land.
itinerary.evening: Kungsbacka's old town on Storgatan for dinner. Short day by design: the first afternoon on a loaded bike is where blisters get decided.

itinerary.title: Kungsbacka to Varberg
itinerary.morning: Tjolöholm Castle, an Arts-and-Crafts manor on its own peninsula, opens at 11:00 in season, the stables café does a good early lunch.
itinerary.afternoon: Through Åsa and Frillesås on quiet lanes, then the long open coast toward Varberg. The last 10 km run past Apelviken, Sweden's most consistent surf and windsurf beach, expect to be overtaken by kite buggies.
itinerary.evening: Varberg. Swim from the Varberg Kallbadhus, a Moorish-style 1903 cold bathhouse on the pier with separate sex-segregated open-air pools and a wood sauna. Dinner in the Societetsparken pavilion.

itinerary.title: Varberg to Falkenberg (32 km) plus Ätran valley loop
itinerary.morning: Varberg Fortress, where the Bocksten Man, a fully clothed 14th-century bog body, is displayed. One hour, genuinely unsettling.
itinerary.afternoon: Short flat coastal ride via Träslövsläge and Ugglarps to Falkenberg. Check in early, then ride the Ätran river loop inland: the Ätran is one of Europe's original catch-and-release salmon rivers and the old town of wooden houses around Tullbron bridge is the prettiest hour on the whole route.
itinerary.evening: Falkenberg has a serious brewing scene; the town's brewery taproom plus a river-side dinner.

itinerary.title: Falkenberg to Halmstad
itinerary.morning: Coastal cycleway via Skrea Strand and Glommen, a working fishing harbour where the smoked prawn stands open around 10:00.
itinerary.afternoon: Steninge and the Möllegård cliffs, then into Halmstad along the Nissan river. Detour to Tylösand, a 7 km white-sand beach that is essentially Sweden's summer capital.
itinerary.evening: Halmstad Castle waterfront, dinner in the Stora Torg quarter, evening swim at Tylösand where the sun sets straight into the Kattegat.

itinerary.title: Halmstad to Båstad over Hallandsåsen
itinerary.morning: South via Trönninge and Eldsberga, gently rolling farmland. Fuel properly in Laholm, the ascent is next.
itinerary.afternoon: Hallandsåsen ridge: a steady 5-6 km climb to about 200 m with a fast, technical descent into Båstad on the Bjäre peninsula. Not steep, but it is where the day is won.
itinerary.evening: Båstad. Tennis town, old harbour, Norrviken Gardens on the headland. Dinner overlooking Laholm Bay.
itinerary.dayStats: 48 km, the route's only real climb

itinerary.title: Bjäre peninsula and on to Ängelholm
itinerary.morning: The Bjäre loop is the best riding on the route: Kattvik, Hovs Hallar's red cliffs (where Bergman filmed *The Seventh Seal*), and the potato fields the Bjärehalvön is famous for. Rolling, hedged, lanes barely wider than a car.
itinerary.afternoon: Down the west side via Torekov and Båstad's back roads, then south through Skälderviken to Ängelholm.
itinerary.evening: Ängelholm Havsbaden beach and a quiet last-but-one night.

itinerary.title: Ängelholm to Helsingborg and out
itinerary.morning: The finest final stretch on Kattegattleden: Rönnen nature reserve, then the cliff-edge cycleway past Domsten and Viken with Denmark two miles across the Sound.
itinerary.afternoon: Arrive Helsingborg. Climb Kärnan tower for the view over to Helsingør. Return bikes, then train north to Gothenburg (about 2 h 15) or the 20-minute ferry to Denmark for a Copenhagen flight.

accommodationStrategy.name: Varbergs Kusthotell
accommodationStrategy.description: Directly on the promenade beside the Kallbadhus, with a spa you will want on Day 2 evening. Secure bike room and a drying cabinet for wet kit. Book a sea-side room, the rail-side ones face the tracks.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel Skansen / Båstad harbour properties
accommodationStrategy.description: Base for the Bjäre loop day. Choose a property in the harbour rather than upper Båstad: after the Hallandsåsen descent you will not want the extra 60 m of climbing home each evening.

accommodationStrategy.name: STF Hostels along the route
accommodationStrategy.description: Sweden's touring club network, clean, cheap, always with a kitchen and a lockable cycle shed, and the standard fallback if you decide to reshape the stages mid-week. Bring or hire bed linen; it is charged extra by default.

logistics.emergency: 112. Hospitals in Varberg, Halmstad and Helsingborg. Sweden's *Trafikverket* road-condition service and the SMHI weather app are both usable in English.
logistics.weather: Southwesterly prevailing wind. A frontal day in Halland means 10-14 m/s straight off the sea with no shelter for 20 km at a stretch. Build one flex day into a 7-day plan or accept a train hop.
logistics.bookingWindows: July is Swedish industrial holiday season, coastal hotels sell out 3-4 months out and prices roughly double. Late August and September are half the price with better riding.

other.label: Signage
other.text: Kattegattleden is Sweden's first national tourist cycle route and is fully signposted with distinctive blue-and-white markers in both directions. Signage is reliable enough that a GPX file is a backup, not a necessity.

other.label: Bikes on trains
other.text: Rules differ by operator and change often: Skåne's Pågatåg and Öresundståg carry bikes with restrictions in rush hour; long-distance SJ services generally require a boxed bike or a booked bike space on selected trains. Plan the return leg before you book, this is the single most common trip-ruining detail on this route. `verify: true`

other.label: Luggage transfer
other.text: Several Halland-based operators run pannier transfer between the standard overnight towns, roughly €20-30 per bag per stage. Worth it if you are riding on a light road bike rather than a tourer.

other.label: Right to roam
other.text: *Allemansrätten* allows wild camping for one night on unenclosed land away from dwellings, but not on the Bjäre peninsula's fenced farmland, and not on the beach reserves, which are explicitly excluded.

proTips: Ride **north to south**. Finishing at Helsingborg gives you a fast train home, a Danish ferry option, and a downhill last day.
The **Kallbadhus at Varberg** is open early. Go at 07:00 on Day 3 before you ride, sauna, cold Kattegat, empty pier.
Swedish *fika* is a logistics tool, not a cliché: bakeries in Falkenberg and Torekov open at 07:00 and close at 15:00. Plan the long afternoon stages with a packed lunch, not a hopeful one.
Hovs Hallar is packed 11:00-15:00 with car tourists. Ride it at **08:30** and you will have the cliffs to yourself.
If a headwind day arrives, take the regional train **Halmstad-Ängelholm** and use the saved hours on the Bjäre loop instead. The Bjäre is the good part; the flat farmland is not what you came for.
Book Tjolöholm Castle's guided tour slot online the night before, the walk-up queue on a July Saturday is over an hour.
